messages:
sam: Hey - noticed a reproducible hang on process shutdown when using async streaming + generator finalizers. App doesn't exit until a few seconds later, socket stays in CLOSE_WAIT. Happens reliably in our sample app.

maya: Ugh. Any logs or a tiny repro? Is this the SSE/HTTP chunked path or our websocket helper?

sam: SSE/chunked path. Minimal repro below (simplified from sample-app):

sam: ```python
async def fetch():
    async for chunk in client.stream.generate(prompt="hi"):
        print(chunk.text)

async def main():
    await fetch()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(main())
```

sam: If you run that and Ctrl-C or let it finish, the process sometimes lingers ~6s. On close it looks like our finalizer for the generator is trying to aclose the iterator while token-refresh background task also races to re-open the connection.

kevin: Could be the weakref finalizer + token refresh thread both trying to close/flush the socket. Which transport are you on (httpx/anyio)?

sam: httpx/asyncio. We saw this on linux and mac. Netstat shows socket in CLOSE_WAIT until finalizer completes. No exceptions logged.

maya: Do you get leaked coroutines or ResourceWarnings? Maybe a bunch of pending tasks hold the loop open.

sam: No ResourceWarning. I added debug prints inside our generator -> __anext__ / aclose paths and it shows aclose being invoked twice: once explicitly from the consumer and once later from the finalizer (weakref) if the generator object is garbage-collected. The second aclose seems to block on awaiting the underlying socket shutdown which may be blocked by auth/token refresh happening concurrently.

andre: Repro sounds plausible. IIRC we call aclose in __del__ via a finalizer, which is risky if the event loop is closed or if there are other tasks. We should avoid running async work from a finalizer; instead schedule a non-blocking cleanup on the loop or rely on explicit aclose only.

kevin: Agree. Two immediate options:
  1) Make finalizer synchronous (close socket with .close() w/o awaiting) and mark a metric, or
  2) Make generator finalizer schedule loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, _aclose()) if loop running and not closed.

maya: Option 2 is better but needs loop liveness checks (loop.is_closed()). Also guard against double aclose (use an atomic flag). We should also ensure token refresh doesn't create a new transport while aclose is in progress.

sam: I hacked a quick patch that sets a _closing flag and schedules aclose on loop if available. Reduced hangs in my manual runs. Will open a PR after some cleanups.

sam: Quick patch gist (pseudo):

sam: ```python
class StreamGen:
    def __del__(self):
        try:
            loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        except RuntimeError:
            return
        if loop.is_closed():
            return
        if not getattr(self, "_closing", False):
            self._closing = True
            loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, self._aclose())
```

kevin: That looks good but be careful: get_event_loop() can return a new loop in some contexts. Use asyncio.get_running_loop() inside try/except and fallback.

andre: Also add a single-run sentinel like _finalizer_scheduled to avoid races across threads. And add a unit test that stubs token refresh to busy-wait while aclose is invoked to ensure no hang.

maya: Can you attach a minimal test to the PR that runs under pytest-asyncio and uses anyio backend matrix? We need to ensure this doesn't regress on uvloop/httpx combos.

sam: Yup. I'll add tests for asyncio + uvloop if CI supports it. Will mark as draft.

sam: Thanks all. Filing the draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/999 (draft). I'll add the flaky test and notes about token-refresh interaction.

andre: One more note — update sample-app README to recommend explicit async context manager usage or explicit aclose to avoid relying on finalizers.

sam: Cool. I'll push updates later today and ping here when draft is ready for review. :rocket:
